sections.html:
Bozeman lies in the Gallatin Valley of southwest Montana, 4,817 feet above sea level. Butte is 84 miles away to the west, Billings 125 miles to the east, and Yellowstone National Park 93 miles south. Interstate 90 passes through. The count in 2020 was 53,293 people, the 2025 estimate is 58,814, and the wider metro area holds about 118,960.

Bozeman Health and Montana State University head the employer list, with firms such as Simms Fishing Products and Mystery Ranch behind them and a growing group of technology and biotech companies. Jobs like these keep newcomers arriving, so a Bozeman house usually draws interest. The questions sellers ask tend to be about tax rates and paperwork rather than demand.

sections.h2: Snow, ice and an older house
sections.html:
Bozeman winters are cold and snowy, summers are fairly warm, and at this elevation the temperature can swing a long way between afternoon and night. Precipitation reaches as much as 24 inches in a year. When a buyer's inspector walks the property, expect attention on the roof's snow load, ice at the eaves and the condition of exterior wood.

A house with deferred repairs does not have to be fixed before it is sold. A cash buyer takes it as is, and the offer accounts for the work still needed. Anyone financing with a loan may ask for repairs after inspection instead.

sections.h2: Who collects property tax, and when it is due
sections.html:
Property tax for Bozeman goes to the Gallatin County Treasurer at 311 West Main, Room 103. Reach the office at 406-582-3030 or treasurer@gallatin.mt.gov, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. For market and taxable value questions, call the Department of Revenue's Bozeman office at 406-582-3400.

PaymentDue date or rule
2026 real property, first halfDecember 7, 2026
2026 mobile home, second halfNovember 30, 2026
Standard state scheduleNovember 30 and May 31, each at 5 p.m.
Late payment2% penalty plus 5/6 of 1% interest per month

Your mortgage servicer or a title company may already be paying on your behalf, so find out before you send a second payment.

Primary residences and long-term rentals get tiered state rates in 2026, starting at 0.76% on the first $378,000 of market value. A second home, short-term rental or vacant residential lot is charged a flat 1.90%, and the Department of Revenue puts VRBO and Airbnb style rentals in that higher class. If you hold a Bozeman-area second home or short-term rental, weigh that rate before deciding whether to keep it or sell.

Someone buying to live in the house can ask for the lower homestead rate. The sale does not hand it over automatically, because the new owner has to apply.

sections.h2: Your three options for a quick sale
sections.html:
Owners here pick between an agent listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. Listing puts the house in front of more buyers and brings showings, commission and post-inspection haggling. Selling alone keeps the commission in your pocket and leaves every form to you. A cash offer is usually as is, with a closing date of your choosing.

The transfer mechanics do not change. A notary acknowledges the deed, the Gallatin County Clerk and Recorder files it with a Realty Transfer Certificate, and recording costs $20 for the first page and $10 for each additional page. Property tax still owed is a lien and gets paid at closing.

Ready for a cash offer on your Bozeman house? Send the address through the form above. A written offer follows, and you owe nothing if you decline.

Selling to a lender-backed buyer means an appraisal, underwriting and frequently a list of repairs. Cash skips all three, so the calendar depends mostly on the title work. Ask for the offer in writing, confirm the closing date, and read the settlement statement for how recording costs and any tax owed are treated.

Two details catch Bozeman sellers off guard. A rental or second home carries a higher tax rate than a primary residence, and the title company has to divide the first and second tax halves between you and the buyer. Raise both early.

• Collect your most recent tax statement and any mortgage payoff figure.
  • Tell the title company whether you or a lender pays the county tax.
  • Check that the names on the deed and on the Realty Transfer Certificate match exactly.
  • Sign the deed in front of a notary.
  • Confirm the clerk and recorder receives the deed, the certificate and the recording fee.
  • Review the settlement statement before funds are released.

None of this is difficult, but each step has a person waiting on it, so starting a week early removes most of the stress. If a lien or unpaid tax turns up, the title company deducts it from your proceeds and the closing continues.

sections.h2: If you owe tax when you sell
sections.html: Late payment brings a 2% penalty and interest of 5/6 of 1% per month, and unpaid tax is a lien on the house. You can still sell. Ask the treasurer's office for the balance, hand it to the title company, and it is paid from your proceeds at closing. Because a cash buyer needs no lender approval, the payoff does not hold up the deal. The Department of Revenue's Bozeman office can answer questions about the value your tax is based on, and the treasurer answers payment questions.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Bozeman?
faqs.a: The Gallatin County Treasurer, at 311 West Main, Room 103. The Department of Revenue's Bozeman office handles questions about market and taxable value.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 property tax rate on a Bozeman primary residence?
faqs.a: A tiered rate: 0.76% on the first $378,000 of market value, 0.90% from $378,001 to $756,000, 1.10% from $756,001 to $1,511,999 and 1.90% above that. Second homes and short-term rentals pay a flat 1.90%.

faqs.q: When is the 2026 first-half tax payment due in Bozeman?
faqs.a: Gallatin County lists December 7, 2026 for the first half of 2026 real property tax. The standard state dates are November 30 and May 31, each at 5 p.m.

faqs.q: Does my Bozeman house need repairs before I sell?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer can purchase it in its present condition. A buyer using a loan may ask for repairs after an inspection.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Bozeman house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. The sale still needs a notarized deed, a Realty Transfer Certificate and recording with the county clerk and recorder.
